Took me long enough to share my account of a very enjoyable Thanksgiving dinner. 😳 Because my friend and I were both Thanksgiving orphans this year, and I was scheduled to lead a Grand Central tour that afternoon, I thought a meal afterward at the @grandbrasserienyc restaurant right in the terminal would be just the ticket. 

Brilliant idea because the food and the cocktails were delicious and the restaurant itself was beautifully-decorated for the holidays.  Marty’s starter was the lobster bisque (in the photo below) and was a meal highlight.  I loved my branzino as well.  It was all great, though, and highly-recommended.

Conveniently, the annual holiday market is next to the entrance to the restaurant, making it easy to pick up a few gifts and follow with a cocktail or a meal.  Highly recommended!

7th Heaven (@7thheavennyc) 
Two great party lineages align for 7th Heaven. Musical hosts Joey Llanos and Douglas Sherman come together in tribute to the collective legacies they represent, a continuation of the musical sensibilities shaped by the Loft and Paradise Garage. Together, they play the music they love and foster an inclusive community that lifts the dancer above the clouds to a place of musical bliss, all night long. 

Joey Llanos (@llanosjoey) is a percussionist-turned-DJ whose relationship with Paradise Garage began when he became head security consultant in 1978. By 1983, he was a backup music selector for Larry Levan. Joey went on to open his own club, The Choice, with Richard Vasquez, and has since slayed dance floors throughout NYC and around the globe. He sits at the helm of the Paradise Garage Reunion parties, alongside Garage legend David DePino, keeping the legacy alive to this day.
 
Douglas Sherman (@baloonwhisperer) has been an integral member of the Loft family dating back to 1979, most notably as David Mancuso’s longest serving back-up musical host. Therefore, it should come as no surprise that he carefully considers the entire experience of a party, from sound quality to decorations. He always has a lineup of extraordinary offerings, a mix of new music and underground classics that he plays with passion and sincerity, driven by his personal connection to the dance floor, rather than merely following a prescribed playlist. His selections are adventurous, joyful, and all encompassing, where every record stands on its own and the music plays us.

Finally tried the famous Honey Butter Pancakes @goldendinerny after waiting almost 3 hours on a beautiful Saturday morning. We arrived right when they opened at 10am and waited about 40 minutes just to get on the list. The host told us the wait for a table (inside or outside — about 58 seats total) would be around 2 hours. Not a problem since I planned to take my niece around to some nearby viral Chinatown spots anyway.

We were seated outside at 12:44pm. We ordered right away and the food came out in about 5 minutes — it honestly felt like the kitchen just continuously makes pancakes and Korean fried chicken since those are the dishes everyone orders. Because of that, everything was lukewarm, not hot, which took away a bit of the “wow” factor for me.

But I do understand the hype around the pancakes:
They’re super thick, really fluffy, and not overly sweet, with a soft, cloud-like interior and a lightly caramelized outside. The honey-maple butter gives a rich sweet-savory flavor that sets them apart from typical pancakes.

We also had:
	•	Korean Fried Chicken Wings

CARAMELIZED PEARS, Brie, Walnuts, Rosemary
.
An absolute BANGER! Need something quick and easy for the holidays? Well here you go friends. Easy to put together, sweet, salty, sticky, crunchy, creamy... Merry Christmas! 🎄 @vitacost #Vitacost #Partner
.
Ingredients:
1 8oz brie cheese
1 pear sliced, I used Anjou
1/4 cup raw walnuts, chopped
1 sprig rosemary
1 cinnamon stick
4 tbsp granulated sugar
2 tbsp unsalted butter
2 tbsp water
sea salt
honey for finishing
.
Directions:
1) Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add sugar and spread it evenly across the pan. Allow it to melt and caramelize slowly, do not whisk or mix it. 
2) After a few minutes when it's melted and golden, add water to thin it out followed by butter, 1/2 the rosemary, and cinnamon stick to infuse. Rotate the pan with the handle, not a spatula. Once melted add pears carefully to the mix.
3) Cook over medium heat for 2-3 minutes then flip pears and cook for another 2-3 minutes. When the pears have softened and are glazed, remove them from the pan to a plate.
4) If the caramel is thick add a splash of water to thin it out. Mix well and add a few spoonfuls to a plate for presentation. 
5) In a small pan, add walnuts and a good pinch of sea salt. Toast over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, constantly mixing so they don't burn.
6) Add brie cheese to the plate with caramel. Top with glazed pears, walnuts, a few rosemary sprigs, and a drizzle of honey. Enjoy!

3 best ingredients with steak?

Pete says onions, mushrooms and garlic.

🍄 Mushrooms – paired with steak in 19th-century French dishes (like Steak Diane). Earthy umami-ness.

🧄 Garlic (in butter) – born of 1930s café de Paris butter. Still a defining steakhouse flavor.

In the last few years that I have diligently gone to check the participating sites in OPEN HOUSE CHICAGO, I have been obsessively posting each one of them that were on my list but this year, I will just focus on one site that was such an astonishing find: The Hawksmoor (https://thehawksmoor.com/us/exceptional-steakhouse/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=&utm_term=hawksmoor%20chicago&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=22551244270&gbraid=0AAAAACfVb1VNgN7dGXycGz5f_vEgT5KHf ) Again, I’m taking an exception in posting this against my ongoing FB/IG abstinence. 

During its former life that dated back to 1887, the 3-story brick building at 500 North LaSalle was the LA SALLE STREET CABLE CAR POWERHOUSE that powered a network of cable cars carrying over 100,000 workers each day. Who knew that Chicago had cable cars then? Everyone who were present during the talk given by local author GREG BORZO who wrote the fully illustrated book CHICAGO CABLE CARS was curiously and pleasantly edified during the Q&A. 

During the 1990’s, the building became MICHAEL JORDAN’S RESTAURANT and just a year ago, it became the Midwest outpost of the London-based HAWKSMOOR STEAKHOUSE named after the 16th century English architect Nicholas Hawksmoor who was a contemporary of Christopher Wren who designed St. Paul’s Cathedral. Now known for its $45 Sunday British Roast, the very friendly staff managed to seat us with only a few minutes to spare to experience this now widely acclaimed HAWKSMOOR  Sunday feast which is a “whole rump of 28-day dry-aged beef that is super-slow cooked, first on real charcoal and finished in the oven. It’s then served alongside the much-loved trimmings: crispy beef dripping potatoes, roasted garlic, buttered greens, carrots, fluffy yet crispy gigantic Yorkshire pudding, cauliflower cheese, all ready to be doused in a Bone marrow gravy.” All three of us decided to get this Sunday special and we are convinced that we shall be coming back for more of HAWKSMOOR.

Join us on October 14th from 7–9 PM at Have and Meyer for an exclusive evening with Chiara Condello, from Azienda Agricola Le Lucciole, a winemaking project, launched in 2015 that represents a deeply personal and terroir-driven vision of Sangiovese.

Working on a small parcel of hillside vineyards in Predappio - soils rich in calcareous clay and fossil-infused “spungone” sandstone - Chiara embraces organic viticulture, hand harvesting, and minimal intervention in the cellar.

Rejecting standardization, she fermentes with indigenous yeasts in gravity-fed vats, uses long macerations, and ages in neutral or older large oak casks, striving to release the silent potency of the land.
 
The result is a pure, expressive Sangiovese that aims to reflect the vintage’s spirit and the soul of Predappio.

Anyway! Came here on a rec from a coworker as what she described as the “Best Burger in NYC”, a statement I do not take lightly. So read along to hear my experience!!

Firstly, the vibe of this place was incredible ! Intimate yet lively and the service was impeccable! Our waiter was great. Now for everyone is actually interested in, the food & drinks!!! 

I can’t find my drink online but it was rlly delicious lol

- hoexters famous Gorgonzola garlic bread 🧄 🧀 🥖 (I personally flinch when I hear the word Gorgonzola, is it just an unattractive name??? Anyway anything with “famous” in the name, I will try. And I am so so happy I did. It was creamy, flavorful, and not overpowering. Definitely would continue to get)
- crispy cauliflower with whipped feta, tumeric, and zhoug (now this. Was. OUTSTANDING. I really really loved this. The zhoug was herby- truthfully I would’ve liked some spice to it- and the whipped feta I was spooning into my mouth alone by the end. Really really good. Not to be skipped.)

Next for mains:
- Hoexters Double Smash Cheeseburger: 
new school american cheese, pickles, special sauce, french fries (this was a really really solid burger. Perfectly cooked. Flavorful sauce. Delish patty. Was it the best burger I’ve had ? I cannot confidently say yes. It was a very very good burger of which I hope to eat again and again but I will not say it is the best I’ve had)
- special ✨❇️: sliced steak sandwich with cheese sauce and onions (guys. Don’t hate me. I think this was better than the burger…it was so. Good. It was like an elevated cheesesteak and I really really enjoyed it - granted I was only given one (1) bite. I would go back for this if I knew when they had it again. It was delicious) 
Also can everyone pls look at the MOUNTAIN 🏔️ of fries 🍟 that come with these dishes?? Omg! Overall, this meal was incredible! Get the cauliflower, get this special (if they have it) and you truly won’t be disappointed in anything else you get!!! Will totally return!

Where did this French classic come from? Legend has it that steak tartare originated from the Mongols, who would tenderize their meat under their saddles, creating a raw dish. However, the French truly brought it to life, turning it into the sophisticated, flavorful delicacy we know today.

At Juliette, we honor this rich tradition by serving ours just as it was meant to be — fresh, simple, and full of flavors. 

As the French would say, “La viande crue, le goût parfait.”
It’s raw, it’s classic, it’s perfection on a plate.

Do you know the story behind the Michelin Man statue at Juliette?

Every piece of history tells a story, and the iconic Michelin Man, or Bibendum, is no different. Born from a moment of observation in 1894, the Michelin brothers, Édouard and André, saw something extraordinary in a simple stack of tires — it looked like a man. This observation sparked the creation of a mascot that would evolve over time, becoming a symbol of quality, innovation, and reliability.

The Michelin Man, originally envisioned as a pile of tires, transformed into the friendly figure we recognize today. From posters and comics to animated commercials, and even as a live mascot, Bibendum’s presence has always reminded us of the power of vision and creativity.

Just like the Michelin Man, each piece here at Juliette holds its own unique history and charm. From our vintage décor to the carefully curated art pieces, every corner has a story to tell.

Each one is a reminder that great things are built on tradition, creativity, and the beauty of time.

Tried @gainblaze for the first time - our initial attempt was nearly 4 hours! 😱 Pro tip: Add your name to the waitlist, and they’ll text you when your table’s ready. You can even track how many parties are ahead, but you’ve got about 10 minutes to check in or lose your spot.

We went on a Tuesday evening, and the place was surprisingly chill at first (almost empty!), though it filled up later—makes sense since it’s a late-night vibe with alcohol on the menu.

The concept is super fun and interactive:
You get a bracelet with a QR code.
Head to the skewer station and grab as many (or as few) as you want—one to sample, or load up!
The best part? Try a single skewer to test flavors before committing to more. (Just remember which is which—it’s on you! 😂)

At the end of the line, the cashier scans your bracelet and inputs each item. The tablet’s mostly in Chinese, and prices vary by skewer, so they double-check closely (we saw them squinting to distinguish beef from lamb 🤣).
.
Then, grill everything right at your table! Timing can be tricky—we’re not taking chances with raw chicken. 😅 Staff are helpful and will flag if something’s done, but when it’s busy, burnt skewers are on you. Seasoning packets on the table add great flavor, though the “melted cheese” side came as one big glob that didn’t quite melt.

Every 10 skewers earns a prize spin. We racked up 20... and won absolutely nothing. 0/2 😂
.
Live music was playing, which elevated the whole vibe—always a win!

Overall, we loved the experience! The food was tasty, the self-paced portion control is perfect, and it’s a fun, unique spot in Flushing’s food scene. Definitely going back.
